Definition: adverb from a derivative of a comparative of G575 and τέμνω (to cut); abruptly, i.e. peremptorily:--sharply(-ness).
BiblicalUsage: The adverb means sharply, abruptly, without softening. Paul tells Titus to rebuke the false teachers sharply so they may be sound in the faith, and he writes sharply from a distance so he will not have to use sharpness when he arrives.
TheologicalSignificance: Sharp words, spoken in love, can be the kindest thing a church hears.
